summary: Role Views — Candidate, Marketer, Supporter, Admin
description:
Build the full set of role-specific page views for all four user types. Each view fetches data from the Spring Boot API using React Query and the configured ApiClient, validates responses with Zod schemas, and renders role-appropriate UI using Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui components. Auth, route guards, layouts, and Zod schemas are complete from Phase 4 Weeks 5-6. This epic wires those foundations to the actual page routes defined in the roadmap.

Candidate routes: /candidate/processes, /candidate/processes/:id, /candidate/sessions/:id
Marketer routes: /marketer/processes, /marketer/processes/new, /marketer/processes/:id, /marketer/sessions/new, /marketer/sessions/:id/status
Supporter routes: /supporter/sessions, /supporter/sessions/:id, /supporter/sessions/:id/feedback
Admin routes: /admin/processes, /admin/questions, /admin/questions/new

Key paths: <apps/web/app/candidate>, <apps/web/app/marketer>, <apps/web/app/supporter>, <apps/web/app/admin>
functionality: navigate role-specific pages to view, create, and manage interview processes, sessions, questions, and feedback
benefit: delivers the full user-facing product for all four roles, completing the Phase 4 milestone

stories.summary: Build Candidate views — process list and session detail
stories.description:
Implement the three candidate-facing pages. The process list shows all processes assigned to the authenticated candidate with session count and technology. The process detail shows a session timeline ordered by round. The session detail shows prep questions ordered by display_order.

Endpoints consumed:
- GET /processes (filtered to candidate's own)
- GET /processes/:id
- GET /processes/:id/sessions
- GET /sessions/:id
- GET /sessions/:id/questions

Key paths: <apps/web/app/candidate/processes/page.tsx>, <apps/web/app/candidate/processes/[id]/page.tsx>, <apps/web/app/candidate/sessions/[id]/page.tsx>

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Candidate sees only their own processes
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated candidate visits /candidate/processes
acceptanceCriteria.then: only processes where the candidate ID matches the authenticated user are listed, each showing technology and session count

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Process detail shows session timeline ordered by round
acceptanceCriteria.given: a candidate visits /candidate/processes/:id
acceptanceCriteria.then: all sessions for the process are shown ordered by round, each displaying status, mode, and scheduled date

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Session detail shows questions ordered by display_order
acceptanceCriteria.given: a candidate visits /candidate/sessions/:id
acceptanceCriteria.then: prep questions linked to the session are listed in display_order ascending, showing body and topic

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Loading skeleton shown while data is fetching
acceptanceCriteria.given: any candidate page is loading
acceptanceCriteria.when: the React Query request is in flight
acceptanceCriteria.then: a skeleton placeholder is rendered in place of the content

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Empty state shown when no processes exist
acceptanceCriteria.given: a candidate has no processes assigned
acceptanceCriteria.then: an empty state message is displayed rather than an empty list

tasks.summary: Define Zod schemas and React Query hooks for process and session endpoints
tasks.description: Create or import interviewProcessResponseSchema and interviewSessionResponseSchema from lib/schemas. Write useProcesses, useProcess, useProcessSessions, useSession, and useSessionQuestions React Query hooks in lib/hooks/ using the configured apiClient singleton.

Create <apps/web/app/candidate/processes/page.tsx>. Use useProcesses hook. Render a card list with technology, status badge, and session count per process. Each card links to /candidate/processes/:id. Show loading skeleton and empty state.

Create <apps/web/app/candidate/processes/[id]/page.tsx>. Use useProcess and useProcessSessions hooks. Render a page header with technology and status. Below, render sessions in a timeline ordered by round — each entry shows round label, status badge, mode, and scheduled date. Each session links to /candidate/sessions/:id.

Create <apps/web/app/candidate/sessions/[id]/page.tsx>. Use useSession and useSessionQuestions hooks. Show session metadata (round, mode, scheduled date, status). Below, list questions ordered by display_order with body and topic fields. Show empty state when no questions are linked.

stories.summary: Build Marketer views — process management and status transitions
stories.description:
Implement the five marketer-facing pages. The process list includes filters for client, status, and technology. The create process form validates with Zod and posts to the backend. The process detail shows all sessions. The schedule session form posts to /processes/:id/sessions. The status transition page shows valid transitions and posts to /sessions/:id/transition.

Endpoints consumed:
- GET /processes (with query params: clientId, status, technology)
- POST /processes
- GET /processes/:id
- GET /processes/:id/sessions
- POST /processes/:id/sessions
- GET /sessions/:id
- GET /sessions/:id/transitions (available transitions for role)
- POST /sessions/:id/transition
- GET /clients (for process form client select)

Key paths: <apps/web/app/marketer/processes>, <apps/web/app/marketer/sessions>

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Marketer can filter processes by client, status, and technology
acceptanceCriteria.given: a marketer visits /marketer/processes and sets a status filter
acceptanceCriteria.then: only processes matching the filter are shown and the URL search params are updated

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Create process form validates required fields before submission
acceptanceCriteria.given: a marketer submits the new process form with a missing candidateId
acceptanceCriteria.when: the Zod schema validates the form
acceptanceCriteria.then: a field-level error is shown and no API call is made

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Successfully created process redirects to process detail
acceptanceCriteria.given: a marketer fills in all required fields and submits /marketer/processes/new
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user is redirected to /marketer/processes/:id for the new process

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Status transition shows only valid next states for the marketer role
acceptanceCriteria.given: a marketer visits /marketer/sessions/:id/status
acceptanceCriteria.then: only transitions permitted for the MARKETER role from the current status are shown as selectable options

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Successful transition shows updated status
acceptanceCriteria.given: a marketer applies a status transition
acceptanceCriteria.then: the status badge on the page updates to the new status and a success toast is shown

tasks.summary: Define Zod schemas and React Query hooks for marketer endpoints
tasks.description: Create or import process and session schemas. Write useProcesses (with filter params), useProcess, useCreateProcess (mutation), useProcessSessions, useCreateSession (mutation), useSession, useTransitionSession (mutation) hooks.

Create <apps/web/app/marketer/processes/page.tsx>. Read clientId, status, and technology from URL search params. Pass as query params to useProcesses. Render a filter bar (controlled select inputs for status and technology, searchable select for client). Render process rows with client name, technology, status badge, session count, and a link to the detail page. Link to /marketer/processes/new.

Create <apps/web/app/marketer/processes/new/page.tsx>. Build a controlled form with candidateId (user search or UUID input), clientId (select from GET /clients), technology (text input), and description (textarea). Validate with createProcessRequestSchema on submit. Call useCreateProcess mutation. On success redirect to /marketer/processes/:id.

Create <apps/web/app/marketer/processes/[id]/page.tsx>. Show process metadata header (client, technology, status, marketer). Below, list all sessions as a table with round, supporter, scheduled date, status, and a link to /marketer/sessions/:id/status for each. Include a 'Schedule Session' button linking to /marketer/sessions/new?processId=:id.

tasks.summary: Implement /marketer/sessions/new page with schedule session form
tasks.description: Create <apps/web/app/marketer/sessions/new/page.tsx>. Pre-populate processId from URL search param. Form fields: supporterId (user select), round (text), mode (select: ONLINE/IN_PERSON/HYBRID), durationMinutes (number), description (textarea), scheduledAt (datetime-local input). Validate with createSessionRequestSchema. Call useCreateSession. On success redirect to the process detail page.

Create <apps/web/app/marketer/sessions/[id]/status/page.tsx>. Show current session status prominently. Render valid next-state buttons based on role (MARKETER can: CANCEL from SCHEDULED or IN_REVIEW; set PASSED, REJECTED, NO_SHOW from IN_REVIEW). Each button opens a confirmation dialog showing current → next state. On confirmation call useTransitionSession. Show success/error toast.

stories.summary: Build Supporter views — session list, question linking, and feedback submission
stories.description:
Implement the three supporter-facing pages. The session list shows sessions where the supporter is assigned. The session detail shows session metadata and question linking UI. The feedback page shows the draft editor with submit action.

Endpoints consumed:
- GET /sessions (filtered to assigned supporter)
- GET /sessions/:id
- GET /sessions/:id/questions (linked questions with display_order)
- GET /questions (for question search/link UI)
- POST /sessions/:id/questions (link question)
- DELETE /sessions/:id/questions/:questionId (unlink)
- GET /sessions/:id/feedback (supporter's own feedback)
- POST /sessions/:id/feedback (create draft)
- PATCH /sessions/:id/feedback (update draft)
- POST /sessions/:id/feedback/submit (lock and submit)

Key paths: <apps/web/app/supporter/sessions>

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Supporter sees only their assigned sessions
acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter visits /supporter/sessions
acceptanceCriteria.then: only sessions where the supporterId matches the authenticated user are listed

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Question linking UI allows search and link
acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter visits /supporter/sessions/:id and searches for a question
acceptanceCriteria.when: a question result is selected and linked
acceptanceCriteria.then: POST /sessions/:id/questions is called and the question appears in the linked list

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Feedback draft can be created and updated
acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter visits /supporter/sessions/:id/feedback with no existing feedback
acceptanceCriteria.when: they type into the editor and save
acceptanceCriteria.then: POST /sessions/:id/feedback creates a DRAFT record and the form auto-saves updates via PATCH

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Submitted feedback is locked and the editor is disabled
acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter has submitted their feedback
acceptanceCriteria.then: the feedback text is shown read-only and the submit button is hidden

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Submit confirmation dialog prevents accidental submission
acceptanceCriteria.given: a supporter clicks Submit Feedback
acceptanceCriteria.then: the feedback is only submitted after the user confirms; cancelling returns to the editor

tasks.summary: Define Zod schemas and React Query hooks for supporter endpoints
tasks.description: Create feedbackResponseSchema (id, sessionId, status DRAFT|SUBMITTED, content, submittedAt). Write useSupporterSessions, useSession, useSessionQuestions, useQuestions (with search), useLinkQuestion (mutation), useUnlinkQuestion (mutation), useFeedback, useCreateFeedback (mutation), useUpdateFeedback (mutation), useSubmitFeedback (mutation) hooks.

Create <apps/web/app/supporter/sessions/page.tsx>. List sessions assigned to the current user. Each row shows process technology, round, scheduled date, and status badge. Link each row to /supporter/sessions/:id.

tasks.summary: Implement /supporter/sessions/:id page with question linking UI
tasks.description: Create <apps/web/app/supporter/sessions/[id]/page.tsx>. Show session metadata. Below, render a two-panel layout: left panel lists linked questions with drag-to-reorder (or number inputs for display_order) and an unlink button. Right panel has a search input that calls GET /questions?q=:term and renders results as linkable items. Link button calls POST /sessions/:id/questions. Include a link to /supporter/sessions/:id/feedback.

Create <apps/web/app/supporter/sessions/[id]/feedback/page.tsx>. Fetch existing feedback. If DRAFT, show a textarea with the current content and a Save (auto-debounced PATCH) and Submit buttons. Submit opens a confirmation dialog; on confirm, calls POST /sessions/:id/feedback/submit. If SUBMITTED, render content read-only with a submitted timestamp. If no feedback exists, initialise with POST on first keypress.

stories.summary: Build Admin views — process oversight and question bank management
stories.description:
Implement the three admin-facing pages. The process list has advanced filters (all fields). The question bank supports client + topic + round + full-text search filters. The new question form creates a question linked to a client.

Endpoints consumed:
- GET /processes (with all filter params: candidateId, clientId, marketerId, status, technology)
- GET /processes/:id
- GET /questions (with q, clientId, topic, round, page, limit)
- POST /questions
- GET /clients (for filter selects)

Key paths: <apps/web/app/admin/processes>, <apps/web/app/admin/questions>

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Admin can filter processes by all available dimensions
acceptanceCriteria.given: an admin visits /admin/processes
acceptanceCriteria.when: they apply filters for client and status
acceptanceCriteria.then: the process list updates to match and the filter state is reflected in the URL

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Full-text question search returns relevant results
acceptanceCriteria.given: an admin enters a search term in the /admin/questions search bar
acceptanceCriteria.then: only questions matching the term in body or topic are shown, using the backend tsvector search

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Question list supports pagination
acceptanceCriteria.given: the question bank has more than one page of results
acceptanceCriteria.then: the next page of results is loaded and the page indicator updates

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Create question form validates and persists
acceptanceCriteria.given: an admin fills in clientId, topic, round, and body and submits
acceptanceCriteria.when: the Zod schema validates and POST /questions succeeds
acceptanceCriteria.then: the user is redirected to /admin/questions with the new question visible

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Inactive questions are visually distinguished
acceptanceCriteria.given: the admin question list includes inactive questions
acceptanceCriteria.then: inactive questions are shown with a muted style and an 'Inactive' badge

tasks.summary: Define Zod schemas and React Query hooks for admin endpoints
tasks.description: Create or import interviewProcessResponseSchema and questionResponseSchema. Write useAdminProcesses (with all filter params), useAdminQuestions (with q, clientId, topic, round, pagination), useCreateQuestion (mutation) hooks. Use pageResponseSchema<T> for paginated results.

Create <apps/web/app/admin/processes/page.tsx>. Render filter controls for clientId (select), marketerId (select), candidateId (text), status (select), and technology (text). All filters are synced to URL search params. Process table shows candidate email, client name, technology, status, marketer email, and session count. Rows link to /admin/processes/:id (reuse the process detail with full data visibility).

tasks.summary: Implement /admin/questions page with search and filters
tasks.description: Create <apps/web/app/admin/questions/page.tsx>. Render a search input (debounced 300ms, updates q param), a client filter select, a topic text filter, and a round text filter. Below, render a table of questions showing client, topic, round, a truncated body, version, and active badge. Pagination controls at the bottom. Each row links to a future question edit page. Include a 'New Question' button linking to /admin/questions/new.

Create <apps/web/app/admin/questions/new/page.tsx>. Form fields: clientId (select from GET /clients), topic (text input), round (text input), body (textarea). Validate with createQuestionRequestSchema. Call useCreateQuestion mutation. On success redirect to /admin/questions with a success toast.
